sentences.text: Ischioceratops was a small, quadrupedal herbivore estimated to reach a total length of about 2 meters.

The name Ischioceratops means "ischium horned face" and refers to the unique shape of its ischium bones, which have a robust shaft resembling a recurved bow that flares into a subrectangular obturator process with an elliptical hole.
This unique shape of the ischium is considered a single autapomorphy unique to all dinosaurs.
Ischioceratops is one of the few known ceratopsian dinosaurs for which no skull fossils have been found.
The animal possessed an elevation on the proximal part of its tail that formed a tail crest, a feature also seen in other ceratopsians.
The genus Ischioceratops was named and described in 2015 by a team of seven researchers including He Yiming and Xu Xing.
The holotype specimen of Ischioceratops was discovered in Kugou, Shandong Province, China.
Ischioceratops is classified within the family Leptoceratopsidae and is distinguished by having nine sacral vertebrae.
Phylogenetic analysis confirms Ischioceratops as a leptoceratopsid with Montanoceratops as its closest relative.
Ischioceratops lived in the Wangshi Group during the late Cretaceous period alongside centrosaurines, saurolophines, and tyrannosaurines.

While one estimate places Ischioceratops living approximately 77.3 to 73.5 million years ago, another recorded time range for the species spans the Campanian stage, from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
